stem: At Solmark Robotics, an `aws_instance` resource's `iam_instance_profile` argument is set to `aws_iam_instance_profile.example.name`. Which statement about the resulting ordering is correct?

choices.text: Terraform infers that the instance profile is created before the instance, based on the instance profile depending on the instance's IP address
Terraform infers that the instance is created before the instance profile, treating the reference as pointing to whichever object is destroyed first
Terraform only creates the instance profile first when the configuration also adds a `depends_on` argument naming it
Terraform infers that the instance profile is created before the instance, from the instance's argument reading the profile's exported attribute

rationale: An attribute reference lets Terraform infer that the resource being read -- here the instance profile -- is created first, purely from the instance's argument reading its exported attribute; no separate reasoning about the profile's own dependencies is needed. Inventing a dependency running the wrong way, from the profile onto the instance's IP address, assumes something nothing in this configuration expresses. Claiming the instance is created first reverses the actual direction: the resource containing the reference (the instance) waits on the resource being referenced (the profile), not the other way around. And the attribute reference alone already establishes the order, so nothing here needs an explicit depends_on added on top of it.
